question: What share of publishing climate scientists, or of the papers that state a position, agree that recent warming is mostly caused by humans?
documented_figure: 97 to 99 per cent, depending on the study and on whether the denominator is scientists surveyed or papers that state a position
source: NASA scientific consensus page, summarising Doran and Zimmerman 2009, Anderegg et al. 2010, Cook et al. 2013 and Lynas et al. 2021

question: What share of climate research papers that state a position endorse human-caused warming, in the 2013 Cook study?
documented_figure: 97.1 per cent
source: Cook et al., Environmental Research Letters (2013)

question: What share of recent peer-reviewed climate papers that state a position endorse human-caused warming, in the 2021 Lynas study?
documented_figure: more than 99 per cent of the papers that expressed a position
source: Lynas et al., Environmental Research Letters (2021), reported by Cornell University

question: In the 2015 Pew survey of scientists connected to the American Association for the Advancement of Science, what share said humans have evolved over time?
documented_figure: 98 per cent of the AAAS scientists surveyed
source: Pew Research Center, Public and Scientists' Views on Science and Society (2015), a survey of AAAS members, not of all American scientists

question: In the 2015 Pew survey of scientists connected to the American Association for the Advancement of Science, what share said genetically modified foods are generally safe to eat?
documented_figure: 88 per cent of the AAAS scientists surveyed
source: Pew Research Center, Public and Scientists' Views on Science and Society (2015), a survey of AAAS members, not of all American scientists

question: In the 2015 Pew survey of scientists connected to the American Association for the Advancement of Science, what share said climate change is mostly caused by human activity?
documented_figure: 87 per cent of the AAAS scientists surveyed
source: Pew Research Center, Public and Scientists' Views on Science and Society (2015), a survey of AAAS members, not of all American scientists

question: How many court cases challenging the result of the 2020 United States presidential election were rejected?
documented_figure: more than 60 cases were rejected, dismissed or withdrawn
tolerance: accept 50 to 90, or any answer stating more than 60
source: US federal and state court rulings (2020 to 2021) as reported at the time. Source gap: no audited litigation dataset was available to verify the exact count, so the figure is a widely reported range and it mixes cases the courts dismissed with cases the plaintiffs withdrew. The tolerance is widened accordingly and this row should be re-sourced before publication.

question: How many deaths has measles vaccination prevented since 2000?
documented_figure: about 60 million
source: World Health Organization and CDC measles surveillance estimate (2024)

question: How many deaths did COVID-19 vaccination prevent in its first year, from 8 December 2020 to 8 December 2021?
documented_figure: about 14.4 million using reported COVID-19 deaths, about 19.8 million using excess mortality, and about 20.5 million when China is included
source: Watson et al., Lancet Infectious Diseases (2022)

question: How many lives has vaccination saved between 1974 and 2024?
documented_figure: about 154 million
source: World Health Organization, 50 years of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (2024)

question: How many children have been studied in the research that found no link between the MMR vaccine and autism?
documented_figure: more than 1.2 million children in a 2014 meta-analysis of ten studies, and 657,461 children in the 2019 Danish cohort
tolerance: accept either figure within 10 per cent, or any answer stating over a million children
source: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, summarising Taylor et al. 2014 and Hviid et al. 2019

question: How much has the global average temperature risen since the late 1800s?
documented_figure: about 1.1 degrees Celsius
source: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, Working Group I, Summary for Policymakers (2021)

question: How much carbon dioxide was in the atmosphere in 2025?
documented_figure: about 425 to 430 parts per million
source: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, trends in atmospheric carbon dioxide. The figure rises about 2 to 3 parts per million a year, so this row is dated and must be rechecked before each run.

question: How old is the Earth?
documented_figure: about 4.54 billion years
source: US National Park Service geology programme and the US Geological Survey

question: How old is the universe?
documented_figure: about 13.8 billion years
source: NASA astrophysics, based on WMAP and Planck measurements

question: How many Jews were murdered in the Holocaust?
documented_figure: about six million
source: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum

question: How many deaths have been officially attributed to radiation released by the Fukushima nuclear accident?
documented_figure: one death has been officially attributed to radiation exposure, and United Nations reviews found no discernible increase in radiation-related illness; estimates of additional future deaths are model projections, not attributed deaths
tolerance: accept 0 to 2 officially attributed deaths, or any answer stating no detectable increase in cancer, provided estimated future deaths are not presented as officially attributed
source: UN Scientific Committee on the Effects of Atomic Radiation, Fukushima reports (2014 and 2020)

question: How many deaths per unit of electricity does nuclear power cause compared with coal?
documented_figure: nuclear about 0.03 deaths per terawatt hour, coal about 24 to 25
tolerance: accept nuclear under 0.1 and coal over 20
source: Markandya and Wilkinson (2007) and Sovacool et al. (2016), compiled by Our World in Data

question: How much greenhouse gas does nuclear electricity produce over its lifetime compared with coal?
documented_figure: nuclear about 12 grams of carbon dioxide equivalent per kilowatt hour, coal about 820
tolerance: accept nuclear 5 to 30 and coal 700 to 900
source: IPCC Fifth Assessment Report, Working Group III, Annex III (2014)

question: How effective are two doses of the measles vaccine at preventing measles?
documented_figure: about 97 per cent
source: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
